passage: Why are there exactly the particles we see, feeling exactly the forces they feel, and why does gravity fit with the rest? Every particle is one vibration of a single kind of string, the way one violin string gives a whole scale. Different notes are different particles, and the graviton is one of the notes, so gravity is not bolted on but falls out of the same object as everything else. The strings need extra spatial dimensions, curled up too small to see, and the shape of the curling fixes which notes exist. That is why the particle table is not arbitrary: it is set by geometry. Remove the extra dimensions and the notes do not close into a consistent set. Change the curling and you change the particle table. The theory has no free constants of its own; every number in physics is to be read off from the geometry. That one framework yields both the graviton and the other forces, which no other candidate does, is the reason to believe the world is made of strings.

The sky looks the same in every direction to one part in a hundred thousand, and space is flat to within a percent. Neither is a coincidence. In the first fraction of a second a field with energy stored in it drove space to expand by a factor of ten to the twenty-six or more. Regions now on opposite sides of the sky were then in contact, so they had time to reach the same temperature: that is the uniformity. The stretching flattened any initial curvature, the way inflating a balloon flattens its surface: that is the flatness. The same stretching blew tiny quantum jitters in the field up to the size of galaxies, seeding the ripples we see in the background glow, with a spectrum nearly but not exactly the same at every scale, tilted slightly toward the large. That tilt was predicted before it was measured, and it was found. Take the field away and you need the uniformity and the flatness as starting conditions. Put it in and both follow, and the ripples with them.

Stars at the edge of a galaxy orbit as fast as stars near the middle, though the visible matter thins out toward the edge. If gravity is Newton's, the mass holding them must extend far beyond the light: a halo of matter that does not shine, several times the visible mass. The same halos explain how galaxies cluster, how light bends around clusters, and the pattern of ripples in the background glow, which needs matter that does not feel light pressure. In the Bullet Cluster two clusters collided. The hot gas, which is most of the ordinary matter, was slowed and left in the middle, while the mass that bends light went straight through with the galaxies. So the unseen mass is not the gas, and it moves as particles that do not collide would. There is a particle, then, weakly interacting and heavy enough to clump. Remove the halo and the rotation curves fall. Make the particle interact strongly and it stays with the gas. Make it light and fast and the small structures never form.

When you measure a particle that is in two states at once, you see one result. Why one? The wave equation never picks. Follow it honestly and the apparatus, and then you, enter a combined state: one branch in which you saw up, one in which you saw down. Each branch continues. The branches stop affecting one another as they entangle with the surroundings, faster than any observation could catch. So you see one outcome because the you that sees it is in one branch, and the other branch holds a you who saw the other. This needs nothing added to the equation: no collapse, no observer, no special role for measurement. It predicts every interference experiment exactly as the equation does, including the return of interference when branches are brought back together in small systems, which is observed. Remove the branching and you must add a collapse rule with a threshold nobody has measured.

Why does a person who has just resisted a plate of cookies give up sooner on an unsolvable puzzle? Self-control draws on one shared store. Every act of restraint, whatever its domain, draws the store down, and it refills with rest and with glucose. So restraint at one task leaves less for the next, whatever the next task is. The store is one thing, not many: resisting food impairs a later persistence task, and holding back emotion impairs a later handgrip task, across domains. A sugar drink between the tasks removes the drop; a sweetened drink with no sugar does not. Remove the first act of restraint and the second task runs at full length. Add a rest and it recovers. The account also says what should not matter: which domain the first task was in.

Why does one pupil get algebra from a diagram and another only from being talked through it? People take in information through preferred channels: seeing, hearing, doing. A pupil's channel is stable, can be found with a short questionnaire, and matches the way that pupil's memory encodes best. Teach to the channel and the material sticks; teach against it and it slides off. That is why a class taught one way has a fixed quarter who fall behind, and why they catch up when the same content is offered through another channel. The prediction is a crossover: visual pupils do better with pictures than with talk, and auditory pupils the reverse. Remove the match and the gain goes. Swap the channel and the same pupil struggles.

Why do people become depressed, and why do the drugs work? Mood is carried by serotonin signalling between nerve cells. In depression the signal is too weak: too little serotonin is released, or it is cleared from the gap too quickly. Drugs that block the clearing leave more serotonin in the gap, the signal strengthens, and mood lifts over a few weeks. That is why the drugs help, why they take weeks (the receptors adjust), and why removing serotonin's building block from the diet lowers mood in people who have recovered. Remove the block and the drug does nothing. Block a different transmitter and the effect is smaller. So depression is a serotonin deficit, and the drug corrects it.

Why did serious crime in the city fall by half in the nineties? Small disorder is a signal. A broken window left unrepaired says that no one is watching and no one cares. People who would otherwise hold back read the signal and act, and the people who would restrain them stay indoors. So disorder invites serious crime through a chain of signals. Fix the small things, repair the windows, remove the graffiti, arrest the fare-dodgers, and the signal is reversed. Serious crime falls, because the people most likely to commit it were the ones reading the signal. The city did this and crime fell, and the fall began in the districts where the policy was applied first. Remove the policing of small disorder and crime should rise again.

Why does no fund manager beat the market for long? A price is a summary of everything known that bears on it. Anyone who knew something not yet in the price would trade on it, and the trading would move the price until the advantage was gone. So at any moment the price already holds all available information, and the only way to beat it is to know something nobody else knows, which lasts only until you trade. That is why managers who did well one year are no better than chance the next: their success was luck. It is why new information moves prices at once and not over days, and why a cheap index fund beats most active funds after costs. Remove the traders who act on information and prices would drift from what the businesses are worth. Add them and the drift closes.

Why do people with Alzheimer's lose memory, and why does it begin where it does? A protein fragment, amyloid-beta, is produced in the brain and normally cleared. In the disease production outpaces clearing, the fragments stick into plaques, the plaques set off a second protein, tau, to tangle inside nerve cells, and the tangled cells die, first in the memory regions, where plaque forms first. Every inherited form of the disease is a mutation in the production or processing of this fragment, and people with an extra copy of its gene get the disease in middle age. So plaque is upstream. Clear the plaque and the tangling and the cell death should slow. Antibodies that clear plaque now exist, and in trials they slow the decline. Remove the mutation and the inherited disease does not occur. Add the extra copy and it does.

Why do teams that write the test before the code ship fewer defects and cleaner designs? Writing the test first forces you to say what the code must do before you say how, so you cannot write code you have not thought through. It forces small steps, since each test covers one behaviour. It makes the code testable, which means loosely coupled, since code that cannot be tested cannot pass through the loop. And it leaves a suite that catches every regression. Teams that switched saw defect rates fall by between forty and ninety percent. Remove the test-first order and the defects come back. Keep the order and the design improves.

Why do humans have a chin, or fear snakes, or find symmetry beautiful? Any trait that is widespread in a species is there because it raised the survival or reproduction of the ancestors who had it. So for any such trait there is an advantage it gave, and finding that advantage explains the trait: fear of snakes because snakes killed those who did not fear them; a taste for symmetry because symmetric mates carried fewer parasites. The method is to ask what the trait is for, work out the advantage, and check that the advantage would have been real in the ancestral setting. Remove the advantage and the trait would have been lost to drift. It was not, so the advantage was there.

Why do the coasts of Africa and South America fit, and why are the same land fossils found on both? The continents ride on plates of the earth's crust that move a few centimetres a year, driven by slow churning in the mantle beneath. The Atlantic opened along a ridge where new crust wells up; the two coasts were once joined and have moved apart. So the fit is not chance, and the fossils lived on one landmass. The account made a risky prediction. As new crust forms at the ridge it records the earth's magnetic field, which reverses now and then, so the seafloor should carry stripes of alternating magnetism, mirrored on either side of the ridge and older with distance from it. The stripes were found. Stop the spreading and the coasts would not fit. Reverse it and the ridge would be a trench.

Why do stomach ulcers come back after the acid is reduced, and why do they clear with antibiotics? A bacterium lives in the stomach lining, tolerating the acid by making an alkaline shell around itself. It inflames the lining, the lining weakens, and acid then eats a hole. Reducing the acid lets the hole heal but leaves the bacterium, so the ulcer returns. Killing the bacterium removes the inflammation and the ulcer does not return. Nearly everyone with a duodenal ulcer carries the bacterium; a healthy volunteer who swallowed it developed an inflamed stomach within days; a course of antibiotics cures what acid reducers only suspend. Remove the bacterium and the ulcer stays away. Leave it and the ulcer recurs.

Why do the finches on the dry island have deep beaks and those on the wet island slender ones? Birds vary in beak shape, and the shape is inherited. On the dry island the seeds are large and hard. A deeper beak cracks them, so deep-beaked birds eat more, live longer and leave more young, and the population's beaks deepen. Some say this is a circle: whoever survives is called the fittest. It is not. The account says in advance, from the seeds, which beak will spread, and that can be checked before any survivor is counted. In the drought of 1977 the finches on the large-seed island were predicted to deepen, and did; when small seeds returned, the shift reversed. Remove the inheritance and the shift does not carry to the next generation. Change the seeds and the direction changes.

Why does adding people to a late software project make it later? Two workings. A newcomer must be taught by the people who know the system, and those people stop producing while they teach, so for weeks the team's output falls before it rises. And work on one system must be coordinated: with n people there are n(n-1)/2 pairs who may need to talk, so each added person adds more coordination than production. The added output arrives late and the coordination cost arrives at once, so a project already late gets later. Remove the training cost, by adding people who already know the system, and the first working goes. Split the work into parts that do not touch, and the second goes. Where neither can be done, do not add people.
